title: EU Looks to Reduce Cheap Hybrid Cars from China
paragraphs: The European Union plans to limit the number of cheap hybrid cars coming into Europe from China.

According to reports in October, the EU will set a limit, or cap, of 350,000 Chinese hybrid and plug-in hybrid cars a year. A plug-in hybrid is a car that has both a gas engine and a battery that can be charged by plugging it in. The new rule could start as early as December 1, 2026. After the first year, the number of cars allowed will rise by 6% each year, and the rule will last for four years.
The limit is much lower than the current number of imports. About 800,000 Chinese hybrids are expected to arrive in the EU in 2026. In 2025, the number was around 300,000.

Chinese companies have quickly become very important in Europe's hybrid market. In the first half of 2026, Chinese cars made up 25% of the EU's plug-in hybrid market and 14% of the regular hybrid market. In 2024, both numbers were only 2%.

One reason for this growth is that the EU had already put extra tariffs on electric cars made in China, but those tariffs did not include hybrids. Because of this, many Chinese carmakers started selling more hybrids in Europe.

However, there is an important exception to the new rule. Chinese-brand cars that are built inside the EU will not count toward the limit. For example, BYD builds cars in Hungary, and Chery builds cars in Spain. This means the rule could encourage Chinese companies to make more cars in Europe.

Maros Sefcovic, the EU's trade commissioner, said the EU must protect its industries and create fair competition. China's Commerce Ministry said the agreement allows Chinese companies to keep exporting, but that it could still take the issue to the World Trade Organization.
